html:
A Jewish teacher from Tarsus in Anatolia, a Roman citizen, who became the most important early missionary of Christianity. His letters are the oldest Christian writings and make up much of the New Testament.

At first a Pharisee who persecuted the followers of Jesus, he had a vision of the risen Jesus on the road to Damascus a few years after the crucifixion and changed sides. He spent the rest of his life travelling through Syria, Cyprus, Anatolia and Greece, founding churches in cities such as Corinth, Philippi, Thessalonica and Ephesus, and writing to them.

His great argument was that non-Jews could join the new faith without following Jewish law on circumcision and food. That opened the movement to the whole Roman Empire and set it on its way to becoming a religion separate from Judaism.

He was arrested in Jerusalem, appealed to the emperor and was sent to Rome. Tradition says he was beheaded there under Nero in the 60s. His ideas on faith and grace shaped Augustine of Hippo and, through him, the Protestant Reformation.
sum: A Jewish teacher from Tarsus in Anatolia, a Roman citizen, who became the most important early missionary of Christianity. His letters are the oldest Christian writings and make up much of the New Testament.
